entries.headline: Redwood AI special warrants trigger deadline penalty
entries.dek: Missing a 90-day filing deadline raises the units issuable under the company's $3.5 million special warrant financing by 10 percent.
entries.caption: A warrant's fine print proves costly as Redwood AI's missed filing deadline increases the units owed to special warrant holders.

sources.title: Redwood AI Provides Update on Special Warrant Financing

unverified_claims: The original special warrant financing's closing, gross proceeds, and the reason the prospectus supplement deadline was missed are stated only in the company's own release.
brief: Redwood AI Corp. (CSE: AIRX) said it did not meet the 90-day deadline to file a prospectus supplement qualifying the distribution of units issuable under its special warrant financing, which closed July 21, 2026. The brokered private placement of 1,663,000 special warrants raised approximately $3.5 million in gross proceeds, with Maxim Group LLC acting as exclusive placement agent.

Under the terms of the special warrants and the agency agreement dated July 16, 2026, missing that deadline triggers a penalty: the number of units issuable per special warrant rises from 1.00 to 1.10, for no additional consideration, taking the total units issuable to 1,829,300 from 1,663,000. Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant exercisable at $2.48 for 60 months.

The units will issue on the earlier of the company filing the prospectus supplement or November 22, 2026, the release said. It gives no further timeline for when a prospectus supplement might be filed.
body: Redwood AI Corp. (CSE: AIRX) (OTCQB: RDWCF) (Frankfurt: Y0N, WKN: A422EZ) said in an October 20, 2026 release that it did not meet the 90-day deadline to file a prospectus supplement qualifying the distribution of units issuable upon deemed exercise of the special warrants issued in its special warrant financing. The brokered private placement of 1,663,000 special warrants closed July 21, 2026 for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $3.5 million, with Maxim Group LLC acting as exclusive placement agent.

The 90-day deadline, which the release calls the Penalty Deadline, was set under the terms of the special warrants and an agency agreement between Redwood and Maxim dated July 16, 2026, entered into in connection with the offering. A special warrant of this kind converts into units of the company once a prospectus qualifying the underlying securities is filed, or on a backstop date if it is not; missing the filing deadline activates a penalty built into the warrant's own terms.

That penalty increases the number of units issuable on deemed exercise of each special warrant from 1.00 to 1.10, for no additional consideration, the release said. Applied across the 1,663,000 special warrants outstanding, the total units issuable rises to 1,829,300 from 1,663,000, an increase of 166,300 units.

Each unit comprises one common share of Redwood and one warrant exercisable at $2.48 per share for 60 months, according to the release. The units will be issued on the earlier of Redwood filing the prospectus supplement or November 22, 2026.
The release does not state a revised date by which Redwood expects to file the prospectus supplement, nor does it give a reason the original deadline was missed.
No further transaction step beyond the November 22, 2026 backstop date for deemed exercise is described in the release.

entries.headline: Noble Mineral closes Lucas Gold Project purchase
entries.dek: The TSX Venture-listed explorer closed its acquisition of the project from Canada Nickel Company and separately received exchange final acceptance for the transactions.
entries.caption: A remote drill site marks the exploration ground Noble Mineral Exploration now controls after closing its purchase from Canada Nickel.

sources.title: Noble Mineral Exploration Acquires Lucas Gold Project From Canada Nickel Company

unverified_claims: The purchase agreement's terms, including any consideration paid for the Lucas Gold Project, are not disclosed in this release and are described only in Noble's September 17, 2026 release.
brief: Noble Mineral Exploration Inc. (TSX-V: NOB) said it has closed the transactions under its Purchase Agreement with Canada Nickel Company Inc. to acquire the Lucas Gold Project, the company announced October 21, 2026. The transactions were previously announced in Noble's news releases of July 13 and September 17, 2026.

Noble said it has received final acceptance from the TSX Venture Exchange for the transactions under the agreement. The release does not restate the main terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement or describe the Lucas Gold Project, directing readers instead to its September 17, 2026 release for those details.

The October 21 release gives no information on the project's location, size or planned work, nor on any consideration paid or use of proceeds. It confirms only that the acquisition has closed and that exchange approval has been obtained.
body: Noble Mineral Exploration Inc. (TSX-V: NOB) (FRANKFURT: NB7) (OTCQB: NLPXF) announced October 21, 2026 that it has closed the transactions under a Purchase Agreement with Canada Nickel Company Inc., under which Noble acquires the Lucas Gold Project. The transactions were previously announced in Noble's news releases dated July 13, 2026 and September 17, 2026.
The company said Noble has received final acceptance from the TSX Venture Exchange for the transactions under the agreement. No further conditions or approvals are described in this announcement.

For the main terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement and a description of the Lucas Gold Project, the release directs readers to the news release Noble issued on September 17, 2026, rather than restating them here.

This announcement discloses no purchase price, share or cash consideration, royalty, or other transaction term, and gives no description of the project's location, size, geology or exploration history. It states no use of proceeds and no next procedural step beyond the exchange acceptance already obtained.

Noble describes itself, in the release's standard company description, as a Canadian-based junior exploration company that holds securities in Canada Nickel Company Inc., among other listed holdings. The release lists H. Vance White, President, as the contact for further information.

Taken together, the two releases Noble points to — October 21 confirming closing and exchange acceptance, and September 17 setting out the terms — mean a reader following only today's announcement sees confirmation that a previously announced acquisition has completed, without the underlying deal terms restated in the same document.

entries.headline: M/I Homes reports lower third-quarter revenue, profit
entries.dek: The homebuilder's net income fell to $66.6 million on revenue of $1.076 billion as new contracts and deliveries each declined 2% from a year earlier.
entries.caption: Framed homes stand under grey skies as M/I Homes reports third-quarter revenue and profit lower than a year earlier.

sources.title: M/I Homes Reports 2026 Third Quarter Results

unverified_claims: The characterization of market conditions and the company's competitive position is the view of CEO Robert H. Schottenstein as stated in the release, not an independent assessment.
brief: M/I Homes, Inc. (NYSE: MHO) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.076 billion, down 5% from $1.132 billion a year earlier, and net income of $66.6 million, or $2.56 per diluted share, compared with $106.5 million, or $3.92 per share, in the third quarter of 2025.

Pre-tax income was $86.9 million, down 38% from $139.8 million, and included $4.7 million of inventory charges; gross margin was 20.9%, or 21.3% excluding those charges. New contracts fell 2% to 1,861 and homes delivered fell 2% to 2,241, at an average closing price of $460,000. The cancellation rate was 12%.

Chief executive Robert H. Schottenstein said the quarter's results reflect 'increasingly difficult market conditions, including higher mortgage interest rates, weaker demand and growing economic uncertainty.' He said the company remains 'well positioned to manage through this current cycle' given its balance sheet and low debt levels. It repurchased $50 million of shares in the quarter.
body: M/I Homes, Inc. (NYSE: MHO), the Columbus, Ohio-based homebuilder marking its 50th anniversary in 2026, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third-quarter revenue was $1.076 billion, down 5% from $1.132 billion a year earlier. Net income was $66.6 million, or $2.56 per diluted share, against $106.5 million, or $3.92 per share, in the third quarter of 2025.

Pre-tax income for the quarter was $86.9 million, down 38% from $139.8 million, a decline the company tied in part to $4.7 million of pre-tax inventory charges taken in the quarter, against $8.9 million for the first nine months. Gross margin was 20.9% as reported and 21.3% excluding the inventory charges.

New contracts for the quarter fell 2% to 1,861 and homes delivered fell 2% to 2,241, at an average closing price of $460,000, with a cancellation rate of 12%. For the nine months, homes delivered fell 4% to 6,361 while new contracts rose 5% to 6,598, against 6,620 and 6,278, respectively, a year earlier.

The company's backlog stood at 2,046 homes at September 30, 2026, down 7% from a year earlier, with a sales value of $1.103 billion, down 9%, and an average sales price of $539,000. M/I Homes operated 246 communities at quarter-end, up from 233 a year earlier.

The company reported shareholders' equity of $3.3 billion and book value of $130 per share, both company records, along with $621 million of cash and equivalents, a homebuilding debt-to-capital ratio of 18%, a net debt-to-capital ratio of 2%, and zero borrowings outstanding on its $900 million credit facility. M/I Homes repurchased $50 million of its shares during the quarter.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, pre-tax income was $280.6 million, against $446.0 million a year earlier, and net income was $213.5 million, or $8.14 per diluted share, against $339.0 million, or $12.32 per share, in the first nine months of 2025.

Chief executive Robert H. Schottenstein said the quarter's results 'reflect increasingly difficult market conditions, including higher mortgage interest rates, weaker demand and growing economic uncertainty,' adding that the company is 'well positioned to manage through this current cycle given the strength of our balance sheet, low debt levels, diverse product offerings and well-located communities.'

The company said it will hold a conference call on October 21, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. ET to discuss the results. The release includes no forward guidance for the fourth quarter or full year beyond the comments attributed to Schottenstein.

entries.headline: China SXT ends additional share purchase right
entries.dek: The Nasdaq company and the purchasers in its October 8 offering agreed to terminate a right to buy up to $12 million more shares or warrants.
entries.caption: A corporate filing closes a narrow financing option as China SXT Pharmaceuticals confirms no further share purchases under its October offering.

sources.title: China SXT Pharmaceuticals Inc Announces Termination of Additional Purchase Right

brief: China SXT Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ: SXTC) said it has entered a termination letter agreement with the purchasers in its registered direct offering announced October 8, 2026. The agreement ends the purchasers' additional purchase right under Section 2.4 of the securities purchase agreement governing that offering.

That right had allowed the purchasers to buy up to $12 million of Class A ordinary shares, pre-funded warrants, or both, within a 30-day window following the offering's closing. Under the termination agreement, the company said the purchasers no longer have any right, claim or entitlement to make an additional purchase under that section.

The company said every other provision of the securities purchase agreement remains in effect, and the securities already issued in the offering are unaffected. The release does not state why the parties agreed to the termination or give any further timeline.
body: China SXT Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ: SXTC), based in Taizhou, China, announced October 21, 2026 that it has entered into a termination letter agreement with the purchasers in its registered direct offering announced October 8, 2026. The agreement, the company said, terminates the purchasers' additional purchase right contained in Section 2.4 of the securities purchase agreement that governed the offering.

Under the original securities purchase agreement, that right had entitled the purchasers to buy up to $12 million of the company's Class A ordinary shares, pre-funded warrants, or a combination of the two, exercisable within a 30-day period following the offering's closing. A right of this kind gives investors in a financing a window to increase their position on terms already fixed in the initial agreement.

With the termination letter agreement now in place, the company said the purchasers 'no longer have any right, claim or entitlement to make an additional purchase' under that section of the agreement. The release states that provision is the one affected by the termination.

The company said all other provisions of the securities purchase agreement remain in full force and effect, and that the shares and any other securities already issued to purchasers under the October 8 offering are not affected by the termination.

This announcement does not restate the gross proceeds, share count or pricing of the October 8 offering, nor does it state a reason the purchasers and the company agreed to terminate the additional purchase right.

There is no stated use of proceeds or further procedural step in this release. It is limited to confirming the termination of the Section 2.4 right and that the securities purchase agreement's other provisions continue to apply.
